page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance provides 64 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 48 MB of shared L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, VNNI, AES, and SHA for vectorized execution and cryptographic processing.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent disk storage needs. Network connectivity is configured with a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned. The configuration does not include discrete GPUs or specialized accelerators, focusing hardware resources entirely on memory-heavy CPU workloads.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance predominantly in the mid-range performance tier. In CPU and system benchmarking, the server recorded a PassMark CPU score of 11,208.37 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,558. Memory subsystem tests showed 56.43 GB/s for large uncached block reads and 40.74 GB/s for writes, sustaining 7.77 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranked in the lower 25th percentile, and medium-sized LLM prompt processing reached 14.73 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated acceleration. By allocating 8 GB per vCPU without the premium cost of dedicated local NVMe drives or GPUs, the instance provides an efficient operational profile for in-memory data structures, caching layers like Redis, relational database systems, and enterprise data processing.

The server contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on external network volumes and a 5 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the middle performance tier for compute and memory operations, delivering a PassMark CPU score of 11,208.37 and achieving 7.77 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 7B parameter LLM inference are comparatively limited. The instance offers a balanced resource model for in-memory caches, relational database hosting, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
